question: trace the dispatcher 0x5bba800's 0x400-exit body at 0x5bb9a60..0x5bba11a and name its operation: whether it is a fourth form of the same ChaCha block function, and how its counter/output contract compares to the SSSE3 (F2), AVX (0x4000-exit) and AVX2 (sign-exit) forms

trace.frame: sub rsp,0x28 at the entry (0x5bb9a60), restored by add rsp,0x28 just before the ret (0x5bba115); ten rsp-relative slots are touched, [rsp-0x80]..[rsp+0x10] (the SSSE3 form's frame is 0x38 bytes, the AVX form's 0x68, the AVX2 form has no frame at all)

input.bytes_read: 0x00..0x30 of the record (three 16-byte rows at +0x00/+0x10/+0x20); bytes 0x30.. of the record are never read
input.counter: the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20]; variants +0/+1/+2/+3 built at 0x5bb9a77, 0x5bb9a8f, 0x5bb9aaa -- each variant row is the loaded counter/nonce row with its first two dwords replaced by the variant counter (pinsrd $0 with the lea result's low dword, pinsrd $1 with its shr 0x20 high dword), one row per block; this is the construction the AVX form uses (vpinsrd), legacy-encoded, where the SSSE3 form builds its rows with movd and shuffle/or merging (its body contains no pinsrd at all)

round_count_gate.parameter: esi = iterations of the round loop; each iteration runs two double rounds (four ChaCha rounds)

round_loop.head: 0x5bb9b40
round_loop.note: the census equals the F2 (SSSE3) and AVX loop censuses on every count; the AVX2 form's loop census is exactly half of it at twice the width

zero_round_path.note: with esi == 0 no round runs: the constant rows are loaded with the doubled sigma at 0x456c50 (each sigma dword doubled), as in the SSSE3 and AVX forms, so the shared epilogue's adds produce exactly initial + initial

encoding.note: every instruction is legacy-encoded (no VEX prefix anywhere, no ymm operand, no vzeroupper), as in the SSSE3 form; what separates this form from it is the instruction floor: pshufb (SSSE3) for the rotate-by-8 step and pinsrd (SSE4.1) for the counter construction -- one feature step above the SSSE3 form's floor, and the dispatcher tests 0x400 after 0x4000 and before bit 9

same: input: bytes 0x00..0x30 of the record at rdi (three 16-byte rows at +0x00/+0x10 and the counter/nonce row at +0x20); the counter is the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20], with +0/+1/+2/+3 variant rows, one per block
round-count contract: esi counts round-loop iterations, each running two double rounds; esi == 0 takes a zero-round path and the output is exactly initial + initial

round loop: the ChaCha quarter-round network -- the rotation census equals the F2/AVX census on every count (32 paddd, 32 pxor, 16 pshufb, rotations 16/12/8/7 at 8 each, pshufd lane rotations 0x39/0x4e/0x93 at 8/8/4); the AVX2 form's census is exactly half of it at twice the width

feed-forward: worked rows are added to the initial rows -- the four constant-row sigma adds just before the merge and twelve in the shared epilogue, the F2/AVX arrangement (the AVX2 form keeps all sixteen in its epilogue) -- and stored as 16 vector stores covering 256 bytes at rdx (four 64-byte blocks)
counter/output contract: the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4, and 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3 -- are stored to rdx; no return value

constants: the same four 16-byte constants with the same reference pattern as the SSSE3/AVX forms -- sigma at 0x4519c0 twice, rotate-by-8 mask at 0x4531c0 twice, swap mask at 0x452ec0 once, doubled sigma at 0x456c50 once (the zero-round path)
structure: no calls, exactly three branches, all internal, and a single ret
different: instruction floor: this form is legacy-encoded like the SSSE3 form (no VEX prefix, no ymm operand, no vzeroupper) but its counter construction uses pinsrd (SSE4.1) -- measured pinsrd-family counts across the four bodies: SSSE3 form 0 (it builds its rows with movd and shuffle/or merging), this form 8 pinsrd, AVX form 8 vpinsrd, AVX2 form 8 vpinsrd -- so the form's floor is SSSE3 (pshufb) plus SSE4.1 (pinsrd), one feature step above the SSSE3 form's; the dispatcher tests 0x400 after 0x4000 and before bit 9
size: 1,722 bytes / 324 instructions against the SSSE3 form's 1,758 bytes / 340, the AVX form's 1,530 / 301 and the AVX2 form's 868 / 173; the round loop is 214 instructions against 217, 189 and 84

frame and stack: a 0x28-byte frame against 0x38 (SSSE3), 0x68 (AVX) and none (AVX2); ten rsp-relative slots ([rsp-0x80]..[rsp+0x10]) of which the four lowest are working slots loaded and stored inside the loop (22 of the body's 45 stack accesses fall in the loop) -- the SSSE3 form (11 slots, 24 in-loop accesses) and the AVX form (14 slots, 34) share this stack-resident pattern, and only the AVX2 form keeps its state in registers (a single red-zone slot, no in-loop access)
zero-round path: loads the doubled sigma at 0x456c50, as in the SSSE3 and AVX forms; the AVX2 form instead loads its two-lane sigma constant and never references the doubled sigma

exit_400.shape: add rsp,0xa8; pop rbx; pop r14; pop r15; pop rbp; jmp -- the dispatcher's frame is fully unwound before the jump, so the 0x400-exit body is entered with the caller's own arguments (rdi, esi, rdx) and its ret returns straight to the dispatcher's caller

direct_transfers.note: every E8/E9 byte hit in .text was validated against its containing FDE's disassembly; the sole direct transfer to the traced body is the dispatcher's 0x400 exit jump at 0x5bbaff8, and there is no call

operation.name: ChaCha block function (SSE4.1 / legacy-encoded form): four blocks in parallel with feed-forward, the state's 64-bit counter advanced by 4
operation.contract: input rdi = a state record of which bytes 0x00..0x30 are read (key rows at +0x00/+0x10 and the counter/nonce row at +0x20, whose first 64-bit word is the counter); esi = round-loop iterations (two double rounds each); output rdx receives 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3, each the sum of its worked state and its initial state -- and the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4; no return value.  The contract is identical to the SSSE3 form at 0x5bba120, the AVX form at 0x5bbb030 and the AVX2 form at 0x5bbb630 in every observable respect
evidence: the body's round constants are the ChaCha constants, the same four 16-byte constants the SSSE3/AVX forms read: the ASCII string "expand 32-byte k" (the sigma row) at 0x4519c0, its exact per-word double at 0x456c50, the rotate-by-8 pshufb mask at 0x4531c0 and the swap mask at 0x452ec0

the round loop is the ChaCha quarter-round network on 32-bit words: paddd/pxor with rotations 16 (pshuflw/pshufhw 0xb1 word swaps), 12 (psrld 0x14 / pslld 0xc), 8 (pshufb through the byte-rotation mask at 0x4531c0) and 7 (psrld 0x19 / pslld 0x7), with pshufd 0x39/0x4e/0x93 lane rotations for the diagonal rounds -- its census equals the SSSE3/AVX census on every count
the entry builds four counter rows from the 64-bit counter at [rdi+0x20] (+0/+1/+2/+3) with lea/pinsrd groups -- four blocks worked in lockstep, one counter step apart

the epilogue is the ChaCha feed-forward: worked rows are added to the initial rows (four sigma adds before the merge, twelve in the epilogue) and stored as 16 vector stores covering 256 bytes, and the counter row is stored back at [rdi+0x20] with the counter advanced by 4

the reduced/other-operation hypotheses fail on the census: the loop performs the full quarter-round network at the full 128-bit width with the family's exact rotation counts -- only the encoding and the counter construction differ from the SSSE3 form, and only the encoding differs from the AVX form's construction
